title: Authorization Strand: policy evaluation engine and runtime guard for API/Console
creator: Lena Morales
description:
Context: RBAC v1 limitations have surfaced in multi-tenant Dedicated and Private customers: evaluation latency for complex role graphs, lack of unified audit correlation between console actions and runtime API requests, and brittle SSO/SAML admin flows. This ticket defines a new "Authorization Strand": a compact policy-evaluation engine plus thin authorization middleware that can be embedded into API gateway, runtime request path, and console backend to provide consistent, auditable, and low-latency access decisions across environments.

Goals:
- Provide a single decision primitive (allow/deny + explain) usable by API, runtime, and console with <2ms median eval for common rules and <20ms p95 for complex policies.
- Emit structured, correlated audit events for every decision with trace IDs linking console actions to runtime calls.
- Integrate with SSO/SAML admin flows to support on-the-fly role mappings, SCIM provisioning hints, and emergency break-glass for owner accounts.
- Support phased rollout that preserves backward compatibility with RBAC v1 JSON role documents.

Non-goals:
- Replacing policy authoring UI in Console (this ticket supplies the backend and APIs only).

Design overview:
1) Policy evaluation engine (pe-engine):
   - DSL: A compact rule language (YAML/JSON) supporting role inheritance, attribute conditions (resource.labels, request.ip, time windows), and dynamic predicates (team membership via upstream idp).
   - Compiled representation: policies are compiled to an optimized decision graph with precomputed indices for role lookups and attribute checks. The compiler emits a small opaque blob versioned by policy-schema v2.
   - Decision cache: bounded LRU per node keyed by (principal, resource, action, session-claims) with TTL and invalidation hooks tied to policy updates and SCIM changes.
   - Explainability: decisions return a concise path of matched rules and a stable decision_id suitable for audit references.

2) Runtime authorization middleware (authorizer-strand):
   - API Gateway hook (http filter): synchronous check on incoming REST/HTTP requests mapping tokens -> principal claims -> decision call to pe-engine. Returns 401/403 with reason headers and decision_id.
   - Runtime request interceptor (gRPC/http internal): a lightweight in-process library for the inference runtime that performs pre-tokenization checks (preventing expensive work for unauthorized requests) and supports async allow-with-conditions when request can be partially admitted.
   - Console backend adapter: decoupled adapter that augments UI actions with semantic context (resource path, UI intent) before calling pe-engine to get more actionable allow/deny and reason strings for admin UX.

3) Audit logging integration:
   - Structured audit events emitted to the observability pipeline with fields: decision_id, timestamp, principal_id, resource, action, matched_rules, decision_latency_ms, request_trace_id.
   - Correlation: middleware attaches decision_id and audit_event_id to the request trace; Console actions include the trace_id in user-facing logs for support.
   - Retention/obfuscation policy: PII fields (email, subject DN) are hashed in logs unless customer config enables full identity logging.

4) SSO/SAML & admin controls:
   - Policy-to-SAML mappings: admin can configure IdP group -> role mapping; pe-engine evaluates both explicit roles and IdP-derived groups.
   - SCIM sync hooks: on SCIM changes, cache invalidations and incremental re-evaluations for affected principals are triggered.
   - Break-glass: emergency owner bypass token (short-lived, auditable) that routes evaluation through a strict expedited path and logs extra metadata to audit sink.

Compatibility and migration:
- Dual-run mode: default runtime loads RBAC v1 roles and v2 compiled policies and evaluates both during rollout; mismatches are logged to a migration dashboard.
- Feature flags: per-customer opt-in to enforce v2 decisions, with a 7-day monitoring window before hard enforcement.

Performance and reliability trade-offs considered:
- In-process evaluation reduces latency but increases binary size and complexity for private/on-prem. We will ship a compact C++/Rust evaluation core with thin language bindings to minimize footprint.
- Centralized decision service eases updates but adds network hop. We will support hybrid mode: local engine with async policy fetch and central policy push for high-availability.
- Decision cache staleness vs. correctness: shorter TTLs reduce drift but increase misses; we'll expose per-customer TTL controls and an aggressive invalidation on SCIM/policy change events.

Observability and SLOs:
- Metrics: decision_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), cache_hit_rate, audit_event_emit_latency, authorization_denials_by_reason.
- SLO: decision p95 < 20ms for 95% of customers in hosted environment; p99 target negotiated per Dedicated contract.
- Dashboards: new Console page showing migration mismatches, recent denials, and top rules by eval time.

Security considerations and review:
- Threats: privilege escalation via ambiguous inheritance, replay of break-glass tokens, log explosion from explain payloads.
- Mitigations: strict token signing with rotation, rate-limited explain outputs, redaction for PII, and mandatory security_review_required for launch.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: build pe-engine prototype + small-bench harness, unit tests for core operators.
- Week 3-5: implement middleware for API gateway + console adapter, integrate audit emitter (dev pipeline).
- Week 6-7: private preview with 2 internal tenants and one Dedicated customer; gather perf and mismatch logs.
- Week 8: opt-in for broader customers and add migration dashboard.
- Week 10: GA opt-out removal after security review and exec sign-off.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Authorization+Strand+Design+v2
- Proto + API sketch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/tree/authorization-strand/proto
- Migration dashboard spike: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ab12/rbac-migration
- Spike bench results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-spike-bench

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Finalize DSL surface: policy authors want a ternary operator for time-based rules — approve?
- Break-glass governance: should break-glass tokens require two-person approval for Dedicated customers?
- SCIM latency: acceptable window for group changes to propagate in Dedicated vs Hosted (30s vs 5m?).

Next steps:
- Tech lead to approve engine language and implementation language (Rust runtime core preferred).
- Security to schedule formal review and threat modeling session.
- PM/Design to draft Console UX for explain & migration page.
acceptance_criteria: pe-engine can evaluate canonical RBAC v2 policy files and return allow/deny+explain within p95 20ms in hosted test cluster
middleware is deployed on API gateway and denies unauthorized requests with decision_id header
structured audit events for every decision appear in observability pipeline and include trace correlations
SCIM change causes cache invalidation and invalidation is visible in migration dashboard
Console displays migration mismatches and allows per-customer opt-in to RBAC v2 enforcement
